combine_pdf.description: Put PDFs and images together as one PDF, in the order you give them: a contract and its signed pages, or a month of receipt photos ready to send to your accountant. Each image gets a page of its own.
combine_pdf.name: combine_pdf

parameters.description: The PDFs and images (JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP or TIFF) to combine, in the order they should appear. Upload them, or pick files or a list of files from earlier steps. Each image is fitted on a page the size of the first PDF's pages, or A4 when there are only images.
parameters.name: files

parameters.description: What to call the PDF, such as October receipts. .pdf is added for you. Leave empty to call it combined.
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: The new PDF, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file, such as an email's attachments or a drive upload.

document_ref.description: The PDF, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same PDF as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

pages.description: How many pages the PDF has.

create.description: Turn rows, text or data into a file you can attach to an email, upload to a drive, or download: a CSV or Excel spreadsheet, a PDF such as an invoice or a report, a text file, JSON, or a calendar invite that adds events to anyone's calendar.
create.name: create

parameters.description: CSV and Excel files are spreadsheets made from rows. A PDF is a finished document, such as an invoice, a quote or a report, laid out from text. A text file holds text. JSON holds data for another system to read. A calendar invite adds events to Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar when it is opened.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: The rows to write, such as the rows a sheet or an earlier step returned. Each row's fields become the columns, and their names the header row.
parameters.name: rows

parameters.description: What the file says. For a PDF, write it in Markdown (# Heading, **bold**, tables) or HTML, and it is laid out on the page for you.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The data to save, such as an earlier step's result.
parameters.name: data

parameters.description: One event, or a list of them, such as the rows of a sheet. Each needs a title (or summary, or name) and a start, and can have an end, a location, a description, a url and all_day. Dates are read in your time zone. Without an end, an event lasts an hour, or all day when its start is a date with no time.
parameters.name: events

parameters.description: What to call the file, such as Weekly leads. The right extension is added for you. Leave empty to call it data (or file, for text). A PDF is named after its title, and a calendar invite after its event (or invite, for several).
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: The new file, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file, such as an email's attachments or a drive upload.

content_type.description: The file's media type, such as text/csv, or text/calendar for a calendar invite.

document_ref.description: The file, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same file as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

edit_image.description: Get a photo ready to post or send: turn it, resize or crop it to a post's size, add a watermark, and save it as a smaller JPG, PNG or WebP, all in one step.
edit_image.name: edit_image

parameters.description: The photo to edit. Upload one, or pick one from an earlier step, such as an email attachment.
parameters.name: image

parameters.description: Turn the photo, such as one taken on its side. A phone photo is already turned upright for you; this turns it from there, before it is sized.
parameters.name: rotate

parameters.description: Square and portrait posts suit Instagram and Facebook feeds, a story or reel fills a phone screen, and wide suits X, LinkedIn and YouTube.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: In pixels. Leave empty to follow the height and keep the photo's proportions.
parameters.name: width

parameters.description: In pixels. Leave empty to follow the width and keep the photo's proportions.
parameters.name: height

parameters.description: When the photo's shape differs from the size: fill the frame by trimming the edges evenly, or show the whole photo with a white border around it.
parameters.name: fit

parameters.description: Your name or logo in a corner, so the photo stays yours wherever it's shared.
parameters.name: watermark

parameters.description: Such as © Acme Store or @acmestore.
parameters.name: watermark_text

parameters.description: The logo to stamp on the photo. A PNG with a see-through background looks best.
parameters.name: logo

parameters.description: Where on the photo the watermark goes.
parameters.name: position

parameters.description: JPG suits photos and opens everywhere. PNG keeps see-through backgrounds and sharp graphics. WebP is the smallest, for websites. Keeping the original's type saves a GIF, BMP or TIFF as a PNG.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: How much to shrink the file. Balanced looks right in a post at a fraction of the size; strong suits a size limit, such as a marketplace's or an email's.
parameters.name: compression

parameters.description: What to call the edited image. The right extension is added for you. Leave empty to keep the original's name.
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: The edited image, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file, such as a social post's media, an email's attachments or a drive upload. Location and camera details are left out.

content_type.description: The image's media type, such as image/jpeg.

document_ref.description: The image, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same image as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

edit_pdf.description: Change a PDF's pages: keep only some of them (which also splits a PDF or takes one page out), add text such as PAID or CONFIDENTIAL, add an image such as a logo or a signature, or turn its pages into images.
edit_pdf.name: edit_pdf

parameters.description: The PDF to edit. Upload one, or pick one from an earlier step, such as an email attachment.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: Keep only some pages makes a new PDF of the pages you choose, which is also how you split a PDF or take one page out. Adding text or an image puts it on top of the pages. Turning pages into images makes one image per page.
parameters.name: operation

parameters.description: The pages to keep, in the order you want them, such as 1-3, 5 or 2-last. Write last for the last page.
parameters.name: pages

parameters.description: The text to put on the pages, such as PAID, CONFIDENTIAL or an invoice number.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The image to put on the pages, such as a logo, a signature or a stamp. A PNG with a see-through background looks best.
parameters.name: image

parameters.description: Which pages, such as 1, 1-3 or last. Leave empty for every page.
parameters.name: on_pages

parameters.description: Where on each page it goes.
parameters.name: position

parameters.description: How big it is on the page. Small suits a reference number or a signature; large suits a stamp such as PAID.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: PNG keeps text sharp. JPG makes smaller files, and suits scanned pages and photos.
parameters.name: image_format

parameters.description: What to call the new file. The right extension is added for you. Leave empty to keep the PDF's name. Images are named by page, such as Contract page 1.png.
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: What was made, kept for 30 days: a new PDF, or one image per page. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file, such as an email's attachments or a drive upload. For images, go through 'documents' with a Repeat for each, or give 'document_refs' to a step that takes several files.

content_type.description: That file's media type: application/pdf, image/png or image/jpeg.

document_ref.description: The new PDF, for a later step that takes a file. When pages were turned into images, the first image.

document_refs.description: The same files as a plain list, for a step that takes several, such as an email's attachments.

documents.description: Every file made, in page order: the one PDF, or one image per page. Each has document_ref, filename, content_type and size_bytes.

pages.description: How many pages the new PDF has, or how many pages were turned into images.

from_base64.description: Turn base64 text an API sent back, such as a signed PDF or a generated image, into a file to attach, upload or read. A data URL (data:image/png;base64,...) works too.
from_base64.name: from_base64

parameters.description: The base64 text, or a data URL. Pick it from the step that returned it.
parameters.name: base64

parameters.description: What to call the file, with its extension, such as contract.pdf. Leave empty and it is named for what it holds.
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: The new file, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file.

content_type.description: What kind of file it is.

document_ref.description: The file, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same file as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

qr_code.description: Make a QR code a phone camera reads, for a link, a ticket number or any short text, as an image to attach to an email, put in a PDF or upload.
qr_code.name: qr_code

parameters.description: What the QR code reads as: a link, such as a booking page, or some text. Up to about 2,300 characters.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: About how wide the image is.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: PNG works everywhere. SVG stays sharp at any size, for print.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: What to call the image. The extension is added for you. Leave empty to call it QR code.
parameters.name: filename

returns.description: The QR code image, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to an email's attachments or a PDF's images.

content_type.description: What kind of file it is.

document_ref.description: The file, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same file as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

width.description: How wide the image is, in pixels.

read.description: Get what's inside a file: the rows of a CSV or Excel sheet, the text of a PDF or Word document and how many pages a PDF has, the data in a JSON or XML file, or an image's size and shape. Works with an upload, an email attachment, or a file an earlier step downloaded.

mock_response.text:
Name,Email,Company
Jordan Lee,jordan@acme.test,Acme Corp
Sam Rivera,sam@northwind.test,Northwind

read.name: read

parameters.description: The file to read. Upload one, or pick a file from an earlier step, such as an email attachment.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: For an Excel file, the sheet to read. Leave empty for the first one.
parameters.name: sheet

parameters.description: For a spreadsheet, use the first row as the column names. Turn this off when it starts straight into data; the columns are then named column_1, column_2, and so on.
parameters.name: has_header

parameters.description: For an XML file, the part to read, such as //item for every item. Leave empty to read the whole file.
parameters.name: part

returns.description: What's inside the file. A spreadsheet's rows are in 'rows', each keyed by its column header (row.Email); a document's words are in 'text' and a PDF's page count in 'pages'; a JSON or XML file's value is in 'data'; an image's size and shape are in 'image'.

examples.text:
Name,Email,Company
Jordan Lee,jordan@acme.test,Acme Corp
Sam Rivera,sam@northwind.test,Northwind

Invoice INV-1042

Desk lamp      2   $84.00
Total due          $84.00

data.description: A JSON or XML file's value: an object, a list, or a single value. In XML, each element's attributes and the elements inside it are its fields, a tag repeated inside one element is a list, and an element holding only text is that text. With a Part to read, the parts found, as a list. Empty (null) for any other file.

headers.description: A spreadsheet's column names, in order. Empty for a document.

image.description: An image's details, as it is seen (a photo taken on its side counts as upright). Empty (null) for any other file.

format.description: What kind of image it is: jpg, png, webp, gif, bmp, tiff or avif.

orientation.description: Its shape: landscape (wider than tall), portrait (taller than wide) or square.

size_bytes.description: The image's file size in bytes.

transparent.description: Whether any of it is see-through, such as a logo's background.

pages.description: How many pages a PDF has. Empty (null) for any other file.

rows.description: One object per data row of a spreadsheet, keyed by column header. Empty for a document.

text.description: Everything in the file as text: a document's words, or a spreadsheet's cells line by line. Empty for an image.

truncated.description: True when a PDF or Word file had more than 10 MB of text: 'text' is the first 10 MB of it, and the rest was left out.

type.description: What kind of file it was.

to_base64.description: Write a file as base64 text, for an API that takes a file inside its request rather than as an upload, such as an attachment in an email API or a document in an e-signature request. Files up to 5 MB.
to_base64.name: to_base64

parameters.description: The file to write as base64. Upload one, or pick one from an earlier step.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: Also give it as a data URL (data:image/png;base64,...), the form an image needs to show inside an HTML email.
parameters.name: data_url

returns.description: The file as base64 text, with its name and type. The whole result can go back into any step that takes a file.

base64.description: The file's contents as base64 text.

content_type.description: What kind of file it is, such as application/pdf.

data_url.description: The same as a data URL, when asked for: data:<type>;base64,<base64>.

unzip.description: Open a ZIP file into the files inside it, such as a batch of invoices sent as one attachment. Each file is ready to read, upload or attach, one by one with a Repeat for each, or all at once. Opens tar archives (.tar, .tar.gz, .tgz) and gzipped files (.gz) the same way.
unzip.name: unzip

parameters.description: The ZIP, tar or gzip file to open. Upload one, or pick one from an earlier step, such as an email attachment.
parameters.name: file

returns.description: The files that were inside the ZIP, each kept for 30 days. Go through 'documents' with a Repeat for each to read or upload them one at a time, or give 'document_refs' to an email's attachments to send them all.

document_refs.description: The same files as a plain list, for a step that takes several, such as an email's attachments.

documents.description: One entry per file, in the order they were zipped: document_ref, filename, the folder it was in inside the ZIP (empty at the top), content_type and size_bytes.

zip.description: Pack files into one ZIP file, to send or upload them together: uploads, email attachments, or files earlier steps created or downloaded. Can make a tar.gz, a tar or a gzip file instead, for a server or tool that asks for one.
zip.name: zip

parameters.description: The files to put in the ZIP. Upload them, or pick files or a list of files from earlier steps.
parameters.name: files

parameters.description: What to call the ZIP file, such as October invoices. .zip is added for you. Leave empty to call it files.
parameters.name: filename

parameters.description: ZIP opens everywhere. tar.gz and tar are what servers and Linux tools expect. gzip packs one file, such as a large CSV export.
parameters.name: format

returns.description: The new ZIP file, kept for 30 days. Give document_ref to a step that takes a file, such as an email's attachments or a drive upload.

content_type.description: application/zip, or application/gzip or application/x-tar for those formats.

count.description: How many files are in it.

document_ref.description: The ZIP file, for a later step that takes one.

documents.description: The same ZIP file as a one-item list, the shape steps that download files return.

size_bytes.description: The ZIP file's size in bytes.

description: Read files, make CSV, Excel, PDF, text, JSON and calendar files, edit images and PDFs, zip or unzip files, make QR codes, and turn files into base64 and back.
